title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical company handbook summary for Redwood employees. It consolidates the most-requested topics for new hires and managers: what it’s like to work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladder expectations, benefits and perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the primary internal tools and access paths. Use this page as a starting point; links to detailed policies and team-specific guides are included in the Appendix.

Audience and intent
- Audience: all Redwood employees and new candidates who have accepted offers.
- Intent: provide a single, navigable reference for People Ops, managers, and engineers on how we organize roles, run hiring and onboarding, and the standard set of benefits and internal tools.

1) Working at Redwood — culture and operating principles
- Mission orientation: engineers and product teams align on delivering reliable, cost-effective LLM inference for customers.
- Key principles:
  - Ownership: ship with monitoring and runbook for production services you touch.
  - Developer-first: optimize for DX, internal tools, and clear APIs.
  - Data privacy by design: minimize PII in dev environments; follow Data Handling Policy.
- Typical day-to-day expectations:
  - Engineers: weekly syncs, async design reviews on RFCs, 1-2 weekly code reviews.
  - Product: weekly prioritization cadences, 2-week delivery sprints.
  - People Ops: quarterly review cycles and continuous onboarding improvements.

2) Roles & career ladders (overview)
- Role families at Redwood (high-level): Engineering, Product, Research/Applied ML, SRE/Infra, DevRel/Docs, People Ops, Sales/CS, Finance/Legal.
- Career ladder structure (example for Engineering):
  - IC levels: E1 (New Grad/Associate), E2 (Software Engineer), E3 (Senior), E4 (Staff), E5 (Principal).
  - Managerial path: EM1 (Manager), EM2 (Senior Manager), EM3 (Director).
- Expectations by level (summary table)

| Level | Scope | Impact | Typical Tenure (yrs) | Key signals for promotion |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| E2 | owns tasks / features | delivers on time, low defects | 1-2 | consistent delivery, reviewers’ feedback |
| E3 | owns larger components | improves quality & performance | 2-4 | drives cross-team projects, mentors others |
| E4 | technical lead across teams | ships architectural changes | 3-6 | recognized expert, technical strategy influence |

- Promotion process (high level):
  1. Candidate prepares self-assessment and evidence with manager.
  2. Manager collects review package (peer feedback, metrics, project list).
  3. Promotion packet submitted to Calibration panel.
  4. Panel decision and calibration notes returned; manager communicates outcome and next steps.
- Resources: People Ops provides role-specific rubrics and example artifacts. See related_pages for detailed ladder templates.

3) Benefits & perks (high-level summary)
- Compensation: competitive base + equity grants; compensation cycles run annually with market adjustments.
- Health & wellness:
  - Medical, dental, vision plans with US / UK equivalents; Redwood covers 80% of individual premiums for standard plans.
  - Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and mental health sessions.
- Leave policies:
  - Parental leave: 18 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (location-dependent).
  - Vacation: flexible paid time off with manager-aligned expectations; recommended minimum 15 days per year.
  - Sick leave and caregiver leave per local law.
- Learning & development:
  - $2,000 annual L&D stipend per employee.
  - 2 discretionary conference days + $1,500 conference stipend when approved.
- Office & remote support:
  - Home office stipend on hire and equipment refresh cycles.
  - Regional office allowances and commuter benefits where applicable.
- Other perks:
  - Monthly wellness allowance, company offsite retreats, team lunches, and milestone rewards.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview
- Hiring principles:
  - Bias-reducing, evidence-based interviews.
  - Focus on problem-solving, system-design (for senior roles), and role-specific practical tests.
  - Interview panels include cross-functional representation.
- Typical hiring flow (summary):
  1. Requisition approved by hiring manager and People Ops.
  2. Recruiter sources candidates; initial recruiter screen.
  3. Technical/role interview loop (2-4 interviews + assignment for most IC roles).
  4. Hiring committee review and offer approval.
  5. Offer extension and negotiation.
- Offer and preboarding checklist (key items People Ops manages):
  - Background check initiation (if required), benefits enrollment window explained, equipment request submitted, preboarding document with first-week agenda.
- Onboarding program (first 90 days):
  - Day 0-1: welcome email, accounts provisioned, hardware shipped, manager 1:1 scheduled.
  - Week 1: orientation session (company mission, security training, product overview), team onboarding (architecture walkthrough, immediate tasks).
  - Month 1: deliver small onboarding project with paired mentor, complete required trainings.
  - Month 3: formal check-in and success plan update.
- New hire checklist (numbered):
  1. Confirm offer acceptance and complete forms.
  2. Verify identity and complete any local compliance steps.
  3. Complete IT access requests for GitHub, Jira, Slack, internal Confluence.
  4. Attend orientation and security training.
  5. Schedule weekly 1:1 with manager for first 90 days.

5) Internal tools & access guide (core list and ownership)
- Primary tools and purpose:
  - GitHub (code hosting): request via IT self-service form; Teams: eng-developer-experience (owner).
  - Jira (task tracking): project access requested by manager in Jira Admin.
  - Confluence (docs): automatic read access for all employees; write access granted per-space.
  - Slack (real-time comms): auto-invite; policy channels and on-call channels exist.
  - Okta (SSO & identity): used for single sign-on to internal apps; set up during Day 0.
  - AWS/GCP consoles: access is gated via role-based IAM groups; request through cloud-accounts-and-networking runbook.
  - Monitoring & alerts: Datadog for metrics, Sentry for errors — on-call rotation and alert ownership documented in eng-sre runbooks.
- Access request procedure (quick steps):
  1. Employee files access request ticket in IT portal with manager approval.
  2. IT/Cloud Admins validate role requirements and grant access.
  3. Employee verifies access and documents missing permissions to manager.
- Sensitive access & approvals:
  - KMS/HSM and production database creds require manager approval + security review.
  - Private deployment artifacts (customer-sensitive) are restricted; follow Secure SDLC and data residency policies.

6) Day 1 / Week 1 manager checklist (practical)
- Before arrival: verify hardware and accounts provisioned; send welcome packet and first-week agenda.
- Day 1: 1:1 welcome, team intros, assign onboarding buddy, walkthrough of codebase and prod dashboards.
- End of week 1: confirm access to repos and ticket system, review initial onboarding project, schedule 30/60/90 day goals.

7) Ownership, escalation, and contacts
- People Ops owner: Ava Chen (people-ops) — primary author for this handbook page and escalation for process questions.
- Hiring process and compensation: contact Recruiting Lead (recruiting@redwood.ai) and People Ops comp partner.
- IT & access: contact it-support@redwood.ai.
- Security & compliance questions: security@redwood.ai.

Appendix: links, templates, and further reading
- Templates and rubrics: see Confluence space /confluence/company-handbook/role-rubrics and /confluence/people-ops/promotion-templates.
- Full benefit plan documents: HR Benefits portal (internal link).
- Detailed onboarding guides per team: search Confluence for "team onboarding" or contact People Ops.

Change log

- 2026-08-15: updated benefits summary and promotion process language to reflect new calibration panel flow.

If you have suggested edits or missing topics, please add an inline comment on this page or email people-ops@redwood.ai.
